blocks.title: The shell: the modes, the antipode, the critical line

blocks.title: The de-framing dictionary and the completeness criterion

rows.label: D1
rows.predicate: The dictionary [chart]: horizon $\sqrt \p\leftrightarrow$ Riemann--Siegel length $\sqrt{T/2\pi}$, half-turn $\leftrightarrow n^{-1/2}$, scale $\leftrightarrow\log n$; a shell of cardinality $\p$ reads $\zeta$ on the line to $T=2\pi \p$, one cycle of the shell, and a height is the scale coordinate of the shell that reads it, its count using residues below $\sqrt{T/2\pi}$ only.

rows.label: D2
rows.predicate: Zero density is shell scale-depth: at $T=2\pi \p$ the smooth Riemann--von Mangoldt density is $\frac1{2\pi}\log \p$, $0.6226,0.9891,1.3556,1.7220$ at $\p=50,500,5\cdot10^{3},5\cdot10^{4}$ [chart]; a substitution under the dictionary, recorded as a consistency, not a test.

rows.label: D3
rows.predicate: Reconstruction residue: the finite-horizon error of the main sum is the Riemann--Siegel remainder $O(T^{-1/4})=O(\p^{-1/4})$ (A3), unconditional, fitted slope $-0.24$ over $t=40\ldots5120$ [approx].

rows.label: D4
rows.predicate: The bare horizon-length sum locates the first zeros: one sign change per zero of $\zeta$ on $[10,55]$, each within $0.5$ of $\gamma_n$, from one or two terms [approx].

rows.label: D5
rows.predicate: Completeness criterion: faithfulness of the de-framing ($N_{\mathrm{crit}}=\mathcal N$ at every height), zero-mode completeness of the on-line spectrum for $v$ over the Weil class (A3), the absence of off-line zeros, and the Riemann Hypothesis are equivalent; an off-line zero $\beta+i\gamma_0$ leaves a residual growing as $x^{\beta-1/2}$ at its height.

rows.label: D6

rows.label: D7

blocks.title: The scale-evolution spectrum from the prime side, and the shell theorem

rows.label: E1

rows.label: E2

The exhibited operator is the Jacobi matrix $\mathbf J_N$ (E9), a realisation every finite real multiset admits; its identification with a discretisation of $\Hh$ is not asserted and used by no row.

rows.label: E3
rows.predicate: Cutoff and semiclassical density: with the space quantum $1_\Omega$ as lower cutoff the Berry--Keating phase-space count is the Riemann--von Mangoldt count, density the shell scale-depth of D2 [chart]; the cell normalisation $1_\Omega^{2}\sim2\pi$ is imposed [chart] (A9).

rows.label: E5

rows.label: E9

blocks.title: The screen reading: the value and its control

rows.label: F1
rows.predicate: \textbf{Turing's count on the shell.} $C\le N_{\mathrm{crit}}\le\mathcal N$ (A4); the hypothesis below $T$ is $\mathcal N(T)=N_{\mathrm{crit}}(T)$, $C=\mathcal N$ the certificate. The shell estimates $\mathcal N$ by the pole-corrected comb count (F8; uncertified at finite depth) and $C$ by the main sum's sign changes (A8); the secular condition reads $\mathcal N$, not $N_{\mathrm{crit}}$. An off-line zero is a phantom: $\mathcal N-N_{\mathrm{crit}}>0$.

rows.label: F2
rows.predicate: \textbf{The screen reading.} By D5 and F1 the classical hypothesis below $T$ is the value $\mathcal N(T)-N_{\mathrm{crit}}(T)=0$, both terms estimated on the shell, the count from the pole-corrected comb (convergent under the hypothesis, uncertified at finite depth), the on-line zeros from the sign changes (exact where certified, A8, and simple). Declared, not derived; E12 uses no Euler product.

rows.label: F3
rows.predicate: The control on the line: the completed Davenport--Heilbronn $\Lambda_f$ is real on the line to $10^{-20}$ [approx]; on $[0,87]$ the argument principle counts $N_f=45$ strip zeros against $C=43$ sign changes, the deficit $2$ opening only in the band of the off-line pair (A5), where $|Z_f|$ dips to $0.357$ without crossing; the constituent $L(s,\chi)$ closes with deficit $0$.

rows.label: F4
rows.predicate: The negative control on the comb side: the secular condition on the generalized comb $\Lambda_f$ (divisor recursion from the coefficients) returns two ``on-line'' roots at the phantom height, $85.65/85.75$ (comb to $4\times10^{5}$), where the line holds no zero; the raw count near the pair drifts with depth, $45.14\to45.73$ at $t=85.9$, and is stable away from it [approx].

rows.label: F5
rows.predicate: The $\zeta$ comb at its own singularity, the pole: at $t=1$ (exact count $0$) the raw count drifts, $+0.09\ldots-1.46$ over depths $10^{4}\ldots8\times10^{7}$, while at $t=15$ it stays within $2\times10^{-3}$ of $1$; the pole-corrected count at $t=1$ falls monotonically, $0.0051\to0.0012$ [approx]. The drift is the pole term of F8: no rounding bound for the raw count is depth-independent (F1).

rows.label: F6
rows.predicate: The Euler-product reading: an Euler product is the signature of a single multiplicative structure; the Davenport--Heilbronn function, a superposition of two, has the self-dual line and the functional symmetry and lacks the product; the screen reading separates the cases by the value $\mathcal N-N_{\mathrm{crit}}$ and places no zero on the line by fiat.

rows.label: F7
rows.predicate: The closure of the quantifier, conditional on A2 (the totality finite) and A10 (the height chart's aliasing carries the zero predicate): heights are residues on the reading shell's cycle, the largest shell the Carrier's, so the quantifier closes at the cycle $2\pi\Omega$ and does no further work within it, the value inside the cycle is F2.

rows.label: F8
rows.predicate: \textbf{The smoothed explicit formula.} Under the hypothesis of no zero to the right of the line, $\sum_{n\le N}\Lambda(n)w(n)n^{-s}/\log n=\Pi_N(s)+J_N(s)$ exactly, $\Pi_N$ explicit and unbounded, $J_N(s)\to G(s)=\log((s-1)\zeta(s)/s)$ off the zeros: the pole-corrected count converges to $\mathcal N(T)$. An off-line zero adds an explicit term $-\Pi^{(\rho)}_N$ (Rem.~\ref{rem:combsettle}), not summed over infinitely many. Observed: the corrected counts settle (D2f, D2g, D3) [approx].

blocks.title: Horizon: the values beyond the embedded reader

rows.label: Z1
rows.predicate: The uniform value $\mathcal N=N_{\mathrm{crit}}$ over the Carrier's cycle, and the value at each height in $(2\pi\sqrt\Omega,\,2\pi\Omega]$: read by the shell whose scale is that height, no embedded Subject; the failing computation is the count at that height from any embedded window. Whether a finite-description proof exists is a question no row poses; positivity (\S\ref{sec:promotion}) is not attempted.

rows.label: Z2
rows.predicate: The heights as Carrier residues: under the frame-covariance of the height chart (A1) each $\gamma$ is a residue on the frequency latitude $L_{\kp+1}$ of the Carrier, its exact index below the resolution of every embedded Subject; finite-precision readings remain available to every Subject for the heights its scale reaches.

rows.label: Z5
rows.predicate: The uniform flatness bound over the shells: with $M(\p)=\max_{j\ne0}\lvert\langle\mathbf1_\Pi,\chi_j\rangle\rvert/(\lVert\mathbf1_\Pi-\bar{\mathbf1}_\Pi\rVert\,\lVert\chi_j\rVert)$ the normalised correlation of the shell's prime indicator with the chart modes, mean removed (floor $1/\sqrt{\p-2}$, C5), the bound $M(\p)=O(\p^{-1/2}\log^{5/2}\p)$; the generalized hypothesis modulo $\p$ implies it [import: \citealp[Ch.~20]{davenport2000}], the converse not asserted. Each shell's maximum is a finite computation (C6), the uniform bound read by no embedded Subject.

B1.name: FRC.Rh.lab_pair
B1.doc: 20:B1 [value] — the laboratory pair `(13, 233)`: nested, `13² < 233`; the two cycles share the quarter-turn core `Q₄` and nothing else, `gcd(12, 232) = 4`, with `5² = −1` on `𝔽₁₃` and `89² = −1` on `𝔽₂₃₃`; and `12 ∤ 232`.

B1.name: FRC.Rh.no_cycle_projection
B1.doc: 20:B1 — no projection of the Carrier's cycle onto the Subject's: there is no surjective homomorphism `C_{232} → C_{12}`, since `12 ∤ 232`.

B1.name: FRC.Rh.lab_pair
B1.doc: 20:B1 [value] — the pair `(13, 233)`: nested, `13² < 233`; both cycles carry the quarter-turn core (`4 ∣ 12`, `4 ∣ 232`; `5² = −1` on `𝔽₁₃`, `89² = −1` on `𝔽₂₃₃`) and share nothing else (`3 ∤ 232`, so `gcd(12, 232) = 4`); the Carrier's cycle does not project onto the Subject's (`12 ∤ 232`); the horizon window `H = 3` is wrap-free on both (`9 < 13`, `9 < 233`).

B2.name: FRC.Rh.window_readback
B2.doc: 20:B2 — below the horizon the reading is frame-exact: on any shell `ZMod q` with `H² < q`, residues `n ≤ H` are the integers themselves and window products read back exactly, so the Subject `𝔽_p` and the Carrier `𝔽_Ω` agree on the window.

B2.name: FRC.Rh.prime_iff_window_irreducible
B2.doc: 20:B2 — primality equals irreducibility in the window: for `2 ≤ m ≤ H` and any shell with `H² < q`, `m` is prime iff it admits no factorisation `a · b = m` with `2 ≤ a, b ≤ H` read on the shell.

B2.name: FRC.Rh.sqrt_sq_lt_prime
B2.doc: 20:B2 — `⌊√p⌋² < p` for a prime `p`: the horizon window `H = ⌊√p⌋` is wrap-free.

B2.name: FRC.Rh.window_readback
B2.doc: 20:B2 — below the horizon the reading is frame-exact: on any shell with `H² < p`, a residue `m ≤ H` is the integer `m`, and the product of two window residues reads back as the integer product.

B2.name: FRC.Rh.factorisation_iff
B2.doc: 20:B2 — primality equals irreducibility in the window: for `m ≤ H` on a shell with `H² < p`, `m` factors as `a · b` with `2 ≤ a, b ≤ H` read on the shell exactly when it factors so as an integer. The statement is the same on every shell above the window — the Subject `𝔽_p` and the Carrier `𝔽_Ω` read the same primes.

B2.name: FRC.Rh.frame_coincidence
B2.doc: 20:B2 — frame coincidence: on the Subject `𝔽_p` and the Carrier `𝔽_Ω`, both above the window `H² < p`, `H² < Ω`, a window residue factors on one shell exactly when it factors on the other.

B4.name: FRC.Rh.zero_slot
B4.doc: 20:B4 — zero-slot, every shell: `Σ_{x ∈ F^×} x^k = 0` on every nonterminal exponent `1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2`, and `= −1` on the full cycle `k = p − 1`.

B4.name: FRC.Rh.zero_slot
B4.doc: 20:B4 — the zero-slot on every shell: over the nonzero residues `x = l + 1`, `l < p − 1`, `Σ x^k = 0` for every nonterminal exponent `0 < k < p − 1`, and `Σ x^{p−1} = −1` on the full cycle.

B5.name: FRC.Rh.slot_complementarity
B5.doc: 20:B5 — slot complementarity, every shell: `Φ(k) = −g^k` is injective on the nontrivial spectral slots `1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2` and maps them onto the nonterminal additive slots `F^× ∖ {−1}`.

B5.name: FRC.Rh.slot_complementarity
B5.doc: 20:B5 — slot complementarity on every shell: `Φ(k) = −g^k` is injective on the nontrivial spectral slots `0 < k < p − 1`, its values avoid `0` and `−1`, and every residue off `{0, −1}` is `Φ(k)` for one such `k`.

B6.name: FRC.Rh.phase_circle
B6.doc: 20:B6 — the phase circle `U_{p+1} = {z : N(z) = 1}` has exactly `p + 1` elements, and Frobenius is inversion on it: `z̄ = z⁻¹` for `N(z) = 1`.

B6.name: FRC.Rh.frobenius_eq_star
B6.doc: 20:B6 — Frobenius on the extension is conjugation: `z^p = z̄` for every `z ∈ F(η)`.

B6.name: FRC.Rh.norm_eq_pow
B6.doc: 20:B6 — the norm is the `(p+1)`-st power: `z^{p+1} = z z̄ = N(z)` in the extension.

B6.name: FRC.Rh.quarter_turn_off_circle
B6.doc: 20:B6 — the quarter-turn `i ∈ F` (`i² = −1`) is Frobenius-fixed and off the circle: `N(i) = −1 ≠ 1`.

B6.name: FRC.Rh.Ext.mul_conj
B6.doc: 20:B6 — `z z̄ = N(z)`: conjugation is inversion on the norm-one circle.

B6.name: FRC.Rh.Ext.conj_inv_of_norm_one
B6.doc: 20:B6 — on the circle `N(z) = 1` the conjugate is the inverse: `z z̄ = 1`.

B6.name: FRC.Rh.Ext.quarter_turn_off_circle
B6.doc: 20:B6 — the quarter-turn `i = −g^κ`, as the element `i + 0η`, is fixed by conjugation and lies off the circle: `N(i) = i² = −1 ≠ 1`.

B6.name: FRC.Rh.Ext.circle13
B6.doc: 20:B6 [value] — on `𝔽₁₃(√2)` (`2` a nonsquare mod `13`): the norm-one circle has `13 + 1 = 14` points among the `169` elements, and Frobenius `z ↦ z^{13}` is conjugation on every element.

B7.name: FRC.Rh.ramanujan_sum
B7.doc: 20:B7 — the flat ground state, in any integral domain with a primitive `p`-th root of unity `ω` (the cyclotomic ledger, `𝔽_q` with `q ≡ 1 (mod p)`, or `ℂ`): the full-modulus Ramanujan sum `c_p(n) = Σ_{a=1}^{p−1} ω^{an}` equals `−1` for every `n ≢ 0 (mod p)`, and `p − 1` at the origin; the mode at the spectral origin carries no prime information.

B7.name: FRC.Rh.ramanujan_sum
B7.doc: 20:B7 — the flat ground state: in a shell `𝔽_q` with a frame (no zero divisors) and an element `ω` of order exactly `m`, the Ramanujan sum `Σ_{a=1}^{m−1} ω^{an}` equals `−1` for every `n ≢ 0 (mod m)`. With `m = p` this is `c_p(n) ≡ −1`: the mode at the spectral origin carries no prime information.

B7.name: FRC.Rh.ramanujan53
B7.doc: 20:B7 [value] — on `𝔽₅₃` with `ω = 16` of order `13`: `c_{13}(n) = Σ_{a=1}^{12} ω^{an} = −1` for every `0 < n < 13`, and `12 = m − 1` at `n = 0`.

B8.name: FRC.Rh.half_turn
B8.doc: 20:B8, 20:B10 — the half-turn arithmetic on every shell of `4κ + 1` elements: `2π ≡ −1` with `π = 2κ`, and `2⁻¹ = 2κ + 1 = −π`.

B8.name: FRC.Rh.trace_eq_one_iff
B8.doc: 20:B8, 20:B9 — the finite critical line: `Tr z = 1` exactly when `Re z = 2⁻¹`; this locus is the fixed locus of `σ = ρ ∘ φ : z ↦ 1 − z̄`.

B8.name: FRC.Rh.card_critical_line
B8.doc: 20:B8 — the critical line carries exactly `p` points: `z = 2⁻¹ + bη`, one for each `b ∈ F`.

B8.name: FRC.Rh.norm_on_line
B8.doc: 20:B8 — on the critical line the energy is `N(z) = ¼ − νb²`.

B8.name: FRC.Rh.Ext.critical_line
B8.doc: 20:B8, 20:B9 — the finite critical line: `Tr z = 1` exactly when `Re z = 2⁻¹ = 2κ + 1`; it is the fixed locus of `σ = ρ ∘ φ`; every `2⁻¹ + bη` lies on it, one point per residue `b` — `p` points.

B8.name: FRC.Rh.Ext.norm_on_line
B8.doc: 20:B8 — the energy on the critical line: `N(2⁻¹ + bη) = (2⁻¹)² − νb²`, with `2 · 2⁻¹ = 1`.

B9.name: FRC.Rh.klein_four
B9.doc: 20:B9 — Frobenius `φ = star` and the functional-equation half-turn `ρ : z ↦ 1 − z` generate a Klein four-group: both are involutions and they commute.

B9.name: FRC.Rh.fixed_frobenius
B9.doc: 20:B9 — the fixed locus of Frobenius is the prime meridian `F` (the elements with `b = 0`).

B9.name: FRC.Rh.trace_eq_one_iff
B9.doc: 20:B8, 20:B9 — the finite critical line: `Tr z = 1` exactly when `Re z = 2⁻¹`; this locus is the fixed locus of `σ = ρ ∘ φ : z ↦ 1 − z̄`.

B9.name: FRC.Rh.fixed_half_turn
B9.doc: 20:B9 — the fixed locus of the half-turn `ρ` is the single point `2⁻¹`, the meeting of the prime meridian and the critical line.

B9.name: FRC.Rh.Ext.klein_four
B9.doc: 20:B9 — conjugation `φ` and the half-turn `ρ` generate a Klein four-group: both are involutions and they commute, `φ ρ = ρ φ = σ`.

B9.name: FRC.Rh.Ext.fixed_conj
B9.doc: 20:B9 — the fixed locus of conjugation is the prime meridian: `z̄ = z ⟺ b = 0`.

B9.name: FRC.Rh.Ext.critical_line
B9.doc: 20:B8, 20:B9 — the finite critical line: `Tr z = 1` exactly when `Re z = 2⁻¹ = 2κ + 1`; it is the fixed locus of `σ = ρ ∘ φ`; every `2⁻¹ + bη` lies on it, one point per residue `b` — `p` points.

B9.name: FRC.Rh.Ext.fixed_half_turn
B9.doc: 20:B9 — the fixed locus of the half-turn `ρ` is the single point `2⁻¹`, the meeting of the prime meridian and the critical line: `ρ z = z ⟺ (φ z = z ∧ σ z = z) ⟺ z = 2⁻¹ + 0η`.

B10.name: FRC.Rh.subject_constants
B10.doc: 20:B10 — the Subject constants on every shell: `π = 2κ` with `2π = −1`; the quarter-turn `i = g^{−κ}` (read as `g^{3κ}`, since `g^{4κ} = 1`) equals `−g^κ` and squares to `−1`; `g^π = −1`; and the Euler identity `e^{iπ} = (g^m)^{m·π} = −1` for every odd `m` — the convention "`e = g^m` on the odd representative `m` of `i`" fixes the parity of the exponent, and the identity uses nothing else about `m`.

B10.name: FRC.Rh.subject_constants
B10.doc: 20:B10 — the Subject constants on every shell: `2π = −1` with `π = 2κ`; `i = g^{−κ} = −g^κ` with `i² = −1`; `g^π = −1`; and `e^{iπ} = (g^m)^{m·π} = −1` for every odd `m` — the convention "`e = g^m` on the odd representative `m` of `i`" fixes the parity of the exponent, and the identity uses nothing else about `m`.

B10.name: FRC.Shell.frame13
B10.doc: 00:C1, 20:B10 on `𝔽₁₃`: the frame `(τ; 0, 1, 2)` of capacity `3` — `2` is primitive (decided).

C2.name: FRC.Rh.vonMangoldt_moebius
C2.doc: 20:C2 — `Λ = μ ∗ log` exactly on the divisor lattice: `Λ(n) = Σ_{d ∣ n} μ(d) log(n/d)`; and the support of `Λ` is the prime powers. (Hardy's limit `R_L → (φ(n)/n) Λ(n)` is the import A3.)

C5.name: FRC.Rh.chi_parseval
C5.doc: 20:E13, 20:C5 — Parseval on the cycle: `Σ_j |⟨v, χ_j⟩|² = n Σ_m |v(m)|²`; the chart modes are complete.

C5.name: FRC.Rh.flatness
C5.doc: 20:C5 — mean-square flatness: for a mean-removed vector `u ≠ 0` on the cycle (`Σ_m u(m) = 0`), the normalised correlations `r_j = |⟨u, χ_j⟩|/(‖u‖ ‖χ_j‖)` with the nonconstant modes satisfy `Σ_{j≠0} r_j² = 1` exactly, so their mean square over the `n − 1 = p − 2` nonconstant modes is `1/(p − 2)`: the root-mean-square correlation is `1/√(p − 2)`.

E1.name: FRC.Rh.scale_shift
E1.doc: 20:E1, 20:E12 — the scale-shift `S : x ↦ g^r x` is a permutation of `F^×` (a bijection, so its matrix on `ℓ²(F^×)` is a permutation matrix, hence unitary) with the power characters `x ↦ x^k` as eigenvectors in the `𝔽_p` reading, `S x^k = g^{rk} x^k`, and its fixed-point count — the trace of its permutation matrix — is `(p − 1)·[(p − 1) ∣ r]`, which carries no prime data.

E1.name: FRC.Rh.character_eigen
E1.doc: 20:E12, 20:E1 — the multiplicative characters of the shell are eigenvectors of the scale-shift in the abstract reading: `χ(g^r x) = χ(g)^r χ(x)` for every `χ : F^× →* ℂ^×`.

E1.name: FRC.Rh.chi_shift
E1.doc: 20:E12, 20:E1 — clause (iii): the scale-shift `m ↦ m + 1` (the residue `g^m ↦ g^{m+1}`) has every chart mode as an eigenvector, with eigenphase `e^{2πi·j/n}` independent of the vector: `χ_j(m + 1) = e^{2πi j/n} χ_j(m)`.

E1.name: FRC.Rh.shift_power_character
E1.doc: 20:E1, 20:E12 — the power characters are eigenvectors of the scale-shift `x ↦ g^r x` in the `𝔽_p` reading: `(g^r x)^k = (g^r)^k · x^k`.

E1.name: FRC.Rh.shift_trace
E1.doc: 20:E12, 20:E1 — clause (iii) in the `𝔽_p` reading: the fixed-point count of the scale-shift, the trace of its permutation matrix: `x ↦ g^r x` fixes every nonzero residue when `(p − 1) ∣ r` and none otherwise, `Tr S^r = (p − 1)·[(p − 1) ∣ r]`; the shell's trace carries no prime data.

E12.name: FRC.Rh.chi_inversion
E12.doc: 20:E12, 20:E13 — clause (i): Fourier inversion on the cycle, `v = (1/n) Σ_j ⟨v, χ_j⟩ χ_j`, with the constant mode carrying the mean, `⟨v, χ_0⟩ = Σ_m v(m)`, so the nontrivial modes carry `v − v̄·1`.

E12.name: FRC.Rh.chi_shift
E12.doc: 20:E12, 20:E1 — clause (iii): the scale-shift `m ↦ m + 1` (the residue `g^m ↦ g^{m+1}`) has every chart mode as an eigenvector, with eigenphase `e^{2πi·j/n}` independent of the vector: `χ_j(m + 1) = e^{2πi j/n} χ_j(m)`.

E12.name: FRC.Rh.scale_shift
E12.doc: 20:E1, 20:E12 — the scale-shift `S : x ↦ g^r x` is a permutation of `F^×` (a bijection, so its matrix on `ℓ²(F^×)` is a permutation matrix, hence unitary) with the power characters `x ↦ x^k` as eigenvectors in the `𝔽_p` reading, `S x^k = g^{rk} x^k`, and its fixed-point count — the trace of its permutation matrix — is `(p − 1)·[(p − 1) ∣ r]`, which carries no prime data.

E12.name: FRC.Rh.shift_power_character
E12.doc: 20:E1, 20:E12 — the power characters are eigenvectors of the scale-shift `x ↦ g^r x` in the `𝔽_p` reading: `(g^r x)^k = (g^r)^k · x^k`.

E12.name: FRC.Rh.shift_trace
E12.doc: 20:E12, 20:E1 — clause (iii) in the `𝔽_p` reading: the fixed-point count of the scale-shift, the trace of its permutation matrix: `x ↦ g^r x` fixes every nonzero residue when `(p − 1) ∣ r` and none otherwise, `Tr S^r = (p − 1)·[(p − 1) ∣ r]`; the shell's trace carries no prime data.

E12.name: FRC.Rh.readout_on_line
E12.doc: 20:E12, 20:B8 — clause (ii) of the shell theorem: every readout `z(θ) = 2⁻¹ + θη` lies on the trace-one line, its real part is the half-turn `2⁻¹`, and `θ ↦ z(θ)` is injective (with `card_critical_line`, a bijection of `F` onto the line).

E12.name: FRC.Rh.readout_slot_index
E12.doc: 20:E12 — the slot index of a nontrivial slot: for `1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2` the index `θ = Φ(k) = −g^k` at which slot `k` is read is neither `0` (the centre `2⁻¹`) nor `−1` (the full-cycle exponent).

E12.name: FRC.Rh.Ext.readout_on_line
E12.doc: 20:E12, 20:B8 — clause (ii) of the shell theorem, no axioms: every readout lies on the trace-one line, its real part is the half-turn `2⁻¹ = 2κ + 1`, and `θ ↦ z(θ)` is injective.

E12.name: FRC.Rh.Ext.readout_slot_index
E12.doc: 20:E12 — the slot index of a nontrivial slot: for `1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2` the index `θ = Φ(k) = −g^k` is neither `0` (the centre `2⁻¹`) nor `−1` (the full-cycle exponent), on every shell and with no axioms.

E13.name: FRC.Rh.chi_orthogonal
E13.doc: 20:E13 — orthogonality of the chart modes: `Σ_m χ_j(m) χ_k(m)̄ = n·[j = k]`, each of squared norm `n = p − 1` (with `chi_inversion`, the `p − 1` characters are an orthogonal basis of `ℂ^{F^×}`; the orthonormal system is `χ_j/√n`).

E13.name: FRC.Rh.chi_parseval
E13.doc: 20:E13, 20:C5 — Parseval on the cycle: `Σ_j |⟨v, χ_j⟩|² = n Σ_m |v(m)|²`; the chart modes are complete.

E13.name: FRC.Rh.chi_inversion
E13.doc: 20:E12, 20:E13 — clause (i): Fourier inversion on the cycle, `v = (1/n) Σ_j ⟨v, χ_j⟩ χ_j`, with the constant mode carrying the mean, `⟨v, χ_0⟩ = Σ_m v(m)`, so the nontrivial modes carry `v − v̄·1`.

E13.name: FRC.Rh.power_characters_not_orthonormal
E13.doc: 20:E12, 20:E13 — the `𝔽_p`-valued power characters are never orthonormal: the self-pairing `Σ_{x ∈ F^×} x^j · x^j` is `0` or `−1`, never `1`, on every odd shell.
